source_name: Česká fintech asociace (ČEFTAS / Czech Fintech Association) — members & events
why_relevant: ~80 member firms (fintechs, banks, law firms, software houses); runs working groups and 'FinTech Mixér' networking events. The member directory is a ready-made actor map for Czech payment innovators, and event topics (open banking, AI, digital assets) forecast where new data and pilots will appear.

source_name: Blue Events — Czech conference portfolio (Retail Summit, sector congresses)
why_relevant: Organiser of the largest Central European retail conference (Retail Summit, 10–12 March 2026, Kongresové centrum Praha, 80+ speakers, 1300+ attendees) plus a sectoral congress portfolio. Retail agendas carry checkout, self-service, cash-handling and payment-acceptance sessions — the merchant-side counterpart to bank sources, and a leading signal for POS/ATM estate changes.

source_name: Global Banking Innovation Forum & EXPO Prague (event listing via 10times)
why_relevant: International banking-innovation event hosted in Prague (21–22 April 2026, Cubex Centrum). Exhibitor and sponsor lists identify vendors actively selling into Czech banks — a supply-side signal for core/card platform migrations.

source_name: Komerční banka careers portal (kb.jobs.cz / kariera.kb.cz)
why_relevant: Job postings at a top-4 Czech bank name the platforms, schemes and projects being staffed (instant payments, card processing, acquiring, SEPA, ISO 20022, softPOS). Volume and role mix over time is a weak signal of platform migration and of internal vs outsourced processing.

source_name: ČSOB careers portal (csob.jobs.cz)
why_relevant: Same weak-signal logic for the KBC-owned Czech bank that also runs the Fintech Challenge with Mastercard and executed the first AI-initiated payment in CZ (Apr 2026 Mastercard release) — hiring here maps agentic-payments and acquiring roadmap.

source_name: Global Payments Europe (Prague) careers — acquiring/terminal roles
why_relevant: GPE is a Prague-based processor serving CZ/SK; postings such as Payment Terminal Support Specialist explicitly reference payment terminals, SoftPOS and the CZ/SK/Malta service footprint — direct weak-signal evidence on terminal estate technology and geographic scope, ahead of any ATM/POS statistic.

source_name: Worldline Czech Republic — company profile & open positions on Jobs.cz
why_relevant: Worldline is a major acquirer/processor in CZ; its Czech vacancy count and role mix is a low-cost proxy for whether it is expanding, migrating platforms, or winding down local operations — relevant to POS acceptance market structure.

source_name: Aggregator job boards for CZ payments roles (Indeed CZ, Jobsora, Prace.cz, Práce za rohem)
why_relevant: Cross-employer view of payments hiring in Prague (Indeed listed ~37 and Jobsora ~24 'payment specialist' roles at time of search). Useful to discover employers not yet in the actor map — small PSPs, ISOs, terminal integrators — rather than for the ads themselves.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom — Czech-language press releases
why_relevant: Scheme-side pilot and partnership announcements localised for CZ, e.g. March 2026 'Česko je v digitalizaci online plateb v evropské TOP 5' and April 2026 first AI-executed payment in the Czech Republic with ČSOB. These releases frequently cite share/penetration figures (Click to Pay, tokenisation) that predate official statistics, and reveal which bank is piloting what.

source_name: Visa Czech partnership announcements (via Visa newsroom and CZ business media pickup)
why_relevant: Visa CZ partnership/pilot news is often surfaced first through Czech media pickup (e.g. Prague Airport Visa Lounge from 1 July 2026) and through bank statements — Partners Banka publicly credits Visa for platform/know-how access behind its all-instant payments proposition. Signals which issuer is switching scheme or launching a new product line.

source_name: Partners Banka corporate site & press page (new-entrant roadmap disclosures)
why_relevant: Newest Czech bank; its own press material and Forbes/Peníze.cz interviews disclose cloud core-banking choice, all-instant payments, and planned crypto/investment/insurance modules — a rare public roadmap that dates future product and volume data.

source_name: LinkedIn company/association pages for CZ payments actors (Czech Fintech Association and peers)
why_relevant: LinkedIn posts by CZ associations, banks and PSPs announce pilots, event participation and hires days-to-months before formal PR; hashtags (#ceftas, #fintech, #fintechengage) cluster the local ecosystem. Highest-latency-advantage weak signal in this cell.

source_name: mistoprodeje.cz — Czech point-of-sale / in-store trade media
why_relevant: Retail point-of-sale trade outlet that interviews payments figures (e.g. Dec 2025 interview with SBK director Roman Kotlán). Bridges the merchant/POS-equipment world and the card industry — useful for acceptance-side and cash-handling signals that bank sources miss.

source_name: ČBA / Karetní asociace pages and ČNB conference calendar (institutional event pointers)
why_relevant: Czech Banking Association's card-association page and the ČNB's conferences/seminars/workshops calendar identify official and semi-official events where payment-statistics methodology and upcoming data releases are discussed — the institutional counterpart to commercial conference agendas.

source_name: Economia events — 'Inovace v platebních kartách' conference series
why_relevant: Publisher-run conference specifically on payment-card innovation; agendas and speaker lists give a media-curated view of what Czech issuers consider next-wave (tokenisation, wearables, instant, softPOS).

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — snapshots of cnb.cz payment statistics pages
why_relevant: ČNB restructured its payment-statistics collection (methodology changes effective 1 Jan 2023 and 1 Jan 2024) and retires/relocates dataset pages; Wayback preserves the superseded series, old ARAD table layouts and withdrawn methodological notes needed for long time-series continuity on cards, ATMs, POS and payment volumes.

source_name: Webarchiv — Národní knihovna ČR (Czech national web archive)
why_relevant: National legal-deposit web archive of the .cz domain: full-domain crawls, selective and thematic collections. Preserves defunct Czech bank, fintech, payment-association and trade-press sites (and their statistics pages) that Wayback covers thinly; the only realistic archive for smaller CZ actors.

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (or.justice.cz) — Czech commercial register & document collection
why_relevant: Statutory filings (účetní závěrka, výroční zpráva) for payment institutions, e-money issuers, acquirers, ATM operators and cash-in-transit firms that publish nothing else. Quantifies private actors' revenue, terminal/ATM fleet commentary and ownership — the only public numeric window on much of the CZ payments supply side.

source_name: dataor.justice.cz — open data of the Czech public registers
why_relevant: Bulk CSV/XML exports of public-register entries (from ~1900 to present), filterable by registry court, legal form and period. Enables systematic construction of a CZ payments actor map (all firms with payment-related NACE/objects of business) rather than one-off lookups.

source_name: ARES — Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (ares.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Aggregation layer merging commercial register, trade register, ČSÚ register of economic subjects and tax data. Canonical IČO resolver and NACE classifier for payment/ATM/POS companies; the entry point for building and de-duplicating a CZ actor map.

source_name: Portál otevřených dat Ministerstva financí (data.mf.gov.cz) — ARES and related datasets
why_relevant: Publisher-side catalogue and API layer for ARES and other MF datasets; documents dataset versioning and distribution formats, which matters when a registry series is restructured.

source_name: Národní katalog otevřených dat — NKOD (data.gov.cz)
why_relevant: National federated catalogue indexing every CZ public-sector dataset (ARES, justice, ČSÚ, ČNB-adjacent). Best single discovery layer for finding statistical datasets whose original landing pages have moved or been withdrawn.

source_name: Merk.cz / Imper CZ — digitised Czech & Slovak financial statements with API
why_relevant: Commercial translation layer that OCRs and normalises Sbírka listin filings (2005–present, ~120k filers/year) into structured revenue/EBITDA/liquidity fields, plus a change API for new and modified entities. Removes the OCR burden of raw registry PDFs for sizing private payment/ATM/POS players.

source_name: Hlídač státu — open watchdog database of Czech entities, contracts and beneficial owners
why_relevant: Free aggregation of registry, contract-register and beneficial-ownership data with an open API. Useful for linking payment/ATM vendors to public-sector contracts (bank/state tenders for terminals, cash handling) and for ownership chains behind CZ payment firms.

source_name: Rejstriky.finance.cz — consolidated registry mirror (OR, sbírka listin, živnostenský rejstřík, DPH, RÚIAN)
why_relevant: HTML-friendly mirror/aggregation of several CZ registers in one record per company; often easier to scrape and to full-text search than or.justice.cz, and preserves records when the primary UI changes.

source_name: ARES.CZ / Firmin.cz — free commercial company-lookup front-ends
why_relevant: Search-engine-visible re-publication layer of registry data; useful for name-based discovery of payment-sector firms whose official register entry is hard to surface by keyword, and for spotting alias/trading names.

source_name: Expats.cz — Czech news in English (banking & payments coverage)
why_relevant: Systematically re-publishes CZ banking/payment facts in English — instant payments adoption, contactless trends, the bank-led CVAK scheme, FX card-fee changes — often citing ČNB or ČBA numbers. Surfaces CZ data to English queries that never reach Czech-language pages, and provides usable one-line stats with attribution to chase upstream.

source_name: ČeskéNoviny.cz / ČTK RSS feeds (and ČTK English service)
why_relevant: National news agency output with structured RSS channels including economy/finance; ČTK is the wire that first carries ČNB, ČBA and bank press releases, and its English service is the main route by which CZ payment statistics enter international coverage.
